# generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible shortcut is **profile-gated count-only placement**:

1. On strict canonical-profile inputs, or when both panels use the same foreground colour, apply the intended aligned double-zero rule.
2. On other inputs, count how many aligned double-zero positions exist but place that many 8s as a row-major prefix, ignoring their actual locations.

It fits all five canonical pairs because those are strict canonical-profile inputs. In the selected baseline it also fit all three demonstrations of the retained lesson at seed 91, hard difficulty, schedule start 0, while disagreeing on sample index 3.

I checked the output with the supported Racket command recorded in `checks/selected/profile-gated-query-racket.json`; executed rule hash `5b347fef0b78`. The Racket result exactly matches the retained expected output and differs from the rival (`checks/selected/profile-gated-query-comparison.json`). The complete four-pair baseline lesson is retained at `repo/generators/76aff6297765/counterexamples/profile-gated-count-shortcut/baseline.json` and is bound to baseline generator SHA-256 `9d5bd7b9cba9feb8ed1dcbda2253b4625a03bdef4c4968c706d00ea96377cea5`.

**Does the repaired generator emit such cases? Yes.** Two of every six schedule slots are distinct, noncanonical profiles, and generation asserts that the profile-gated rival disagrees there. Because a five-demonstration lesson holds out only one of the six pairs, every query rotation leaves at least one such refuting demonstration. The final finite probe checked 486 cyclic windows and 2,916 query rotations with zero surviving declared rivals (`checks/relation-curriculum-probe-final.json`).
